media: generated image/video; synthetic fixtures for instrument

media: generated image/video; synthetic fixtures for instrument

required_metadata: prompt-declared action; observation unit = whole clip
label_trust: requires human or qualified VLM adjudication; NOT deterministic

why: The stimulus is Eval's own generation. Resources supplies no media.

required_metadata: requested duration/aspect/resolution/output contract vs delivered
why: This is a file-property check against the request. It needs no reference media at all.

media: generated image/video; deterministic rendered calibration pack for instrument
required_metadata: exact target string; rendered ground truth
independence: string-level; base strings must not be reused between calibration and qualification
resources_note: The corpus holds only 14 English-labelled BSTD images. That is nowhere near a real-world Latin scene-text pool, and it is not needed: the Devanagari battery proved rendered strings are the better instrument.
why: Copying the proven EVAL-005 method to Latin is cheaper and more auditable than acquiring real Latin scene text.

target_quantity: reading: existing 29,722-item pool; rendering: 96-item frozen battery
required_metadata: human transcription per item; script-level filter, not language label
label_trust: source transcriptions are OBSERVATIONS of one annotator group, not project ground truth, until Eval validates them
independence: source lineage: CVIT pair = one lineage; BSTD = independent
rights_minimum: internal research/evaluation only; CVIT sources rights not_stated
resources_note: TWO DIFFERENT ABILITIES, one capability id. Reading real signage is covered. Judging a generator's own Devanagari rendering is covered by the 96-item battery. What is NOT covered is real generated-Devanagari failure material at scale, which only paid generation produces.
why: The single best-covered capability in the project, and the only one where existing material is genuinely sufficient.

required_metadata: type size/contrast/placement conditions declared by the item
resources_note: Canon holds no accepted Devanagari-structure source (CANON-008 stopped). Resources cannot supply typographic judgement criteria and must not invent them.
why: Legibility is judged on Eval's own outputs against declared conditions.

target_quantity: >=12 distinct marks with clear ownership (aligned to the 12 products)
required_metadata: vector or high-resolution original; ownership/permission record; colour spec
independence: brand-level: a mark used in calibration must not appear in qualification
rights_minimum: first-party or explicitly permissioned; third-party trademarks are NOT usable by default
resources_note: PARTIAL, and this is a real find. Three first-party logo assets are recoverable from chawlavaibhav/media-factory git history (spike/refs/logo_0.png, logo_1.png, aight_logo.png). That is 3 of >=12 marks, from a project-owned source. See LEGACY-EVIDENCE-RECONCILIATION.md.
why: Brand fidelity is the capability most exposed to trademark risk. Using project-owned marks removes that risk entirely for the part it covers.

required_metadata: measured or specified brand colour values; lighting conditions recorded
rights_minimum: first-party or permissioned; controlled capture strongly preferred
why: Colour fidelity needs a known reference value. A web image with unknown colour management cannot serve as one.

media: controlled person reference images + generated output
required_metadata: identity id, view/pose/lighting condition, capture date, written consent record
label_trust: known-match/known-nonmatch by construction; similarity is NOT exactness and needs human adjudication
independence: identity-level: an identity in calibration must not appear in qualification
geo_language: should include South Asian faces; skin-tone and age spread recorded
rights_minimum: explicit written consent for internal evaluation use; biometric-data implications documented
resources_note: HIGHEST-RISK ROW IN THE MATRIX. Consent and biometric exposure make this the one pack that must never be filled opportunistically. 19 images of what appears to be a single identity are recoverable from media-factory history, but I could not establish a consent record for them in this session, so they are recorded as a candidate needing rights confirmation, NOT as supply.
why: Identity consistency is a core commercial requirement (the same spokesperson across a campaign) and cannot be measured without controlled references.

media: controlled product reference images + generated output
required_metadata: product id, view/angle, lighting, scale reference, ownership record
why: The single most commercially load-bearing capability: if the generated product is not the customer's product, nothing else about the asset matters.

required_metadata: which reference images were supplied to the model; conditioning mode
why: Measures whether the model actually used the reference it was given. Needs no new media beyond the two packs.

media: both reference packs + controlled edit pairs
required_metadata: before/after pair, declared edit instruction, declared must-not-change regions
why: Editing is where the money is in production reuse. Preservation is checkable against a declared unchanged region, so it is cheap once the packs exist.

required_metadata: declared hand-involving action; observation unit = frame or image
label_trust: human adjudication; no deterministic checker exists
resources_note: Instrument qualification for this needs known-defect examples. Those come from Eval's own generations once E7 runs, not from an acquisition.
why: Classic generator failure mode; the stimulus is the generator's own output.

required_metadata: declared contact/grip relationship
why: Person-holding-product is the commonest commercial shot and the commonest physical failure. Stimulus is Eval-generated.

required_metadata: declared interaction
why: Same pattern as 15/16.

media: generated video; real and generated video for instrument development
required_metadata: per-clip motion/dynamic-degree scores where available
label_trust: VideoFeedback dynamic-degree scores are the distributor's human ratings — observations, not our truth
independence: source lineage: single distributor per pool
rights_minimum: apache-2.0 asserted by publisher; internal evaluation only
resources_note: Useful for DEVELOPING a motion evaluator, not for qualifying one against current models: ImageRewardDB is DiffusionDB-era and VideoFeedback does not even name its generators. Generator era is a real limitation, not a caveat to wave through.
why: This is the one realism capability where existing material genuinely helps.

required_metadata: declared material/physical condition
why: Stimulus is Eval-generated; no reference corpus would establish what 'correct' looks like for an invented scene.

required_metadata: reference identity; sampled-frame observation rule
resources_note: OBSERVATION-UNIT RULE: frames sampled from one clip are ONE trial, not many. Resources records this because a manifest that lists frames as items would silently inflate every count downstream.
why: Face drift within a single clip is a known, recorded failure in this project's own legacy evidence (see LEGACY-MF-SCORES).

required_metadata: reference product; sampled-frame observation rule
why: Same as 20, for the object rather than the person.

target_quantity: reuses PACK-PRODUCT-REF logo subset; Devanagari-in-video has no reference pool
required_metadata: reference mark; target string; per-sampled-frame reading
resources_note: THE SHARPEST GAP IN THE PROJECT. Text that drifts within a single clip is the named commercial failure mode, and the corpus contains no generated Devanagari at all. No acquisition fixes this — only paid generation produces it. Recorded so nobody tries to buy their way out.
why: Reading real signage (REQ-CAP-07) does not test this and must not be reported as if it did.

media: generated multi-shot video; clean base clips for instrument perturbation
required_metadata: shot boundaries; declared continuity constraints
label_trust: deterministic for introduced perturbations; human for natural cases
resources_note: Existing clips can host a KNOWN introduced discontinuity, which is enough to qualify a temporal instrument. They cannot represent multi-shot branded advertising, which needs PACK-COMMERCIAL.
why: Splits cleanly into an instrument need (covered) and a content need (missing).

required_metadata: verbatim transcript; language/code-switching marking
label_trust: transcript must be verified, not distributor-asserted
rights_minimum: voice and identity permissions recorded SEPARATELY from media rights
resources_note: Corpus audio holdings: zero. Not low — zero.
why: Hinglish code-switching is a first-product requirement and no public pack we have reviewed covers it with verified transcripts.

required_metadata: transcript; frame-accurate audio alignment; known synthetic offsets for calibration
resources_note: Eval's own instruction stands: never invent a millisecond tolerance without evidence. Resources supplies the clips and the known offsets; the tolerance is Eval's to derive.
why: Lip-sync is a whole product lane (dedicated lip-sync/digital-human endpoints) with no material behind it.

required_metadata: transcript PLUS turn boundaries with speaker attribution
label_trust: turn boundaries must be verified; a swapped-channel control is deterministic
why: The hardest AV row: turn boundaries are extra annotation that almost no public source ships, and both speakers need permission.

media: AV clips with controlled prosody variants
required_metadata: declared intended register; controlled variants where feasible
label_trust: human adjudication; Resources must NOT author emotional labels
resources_note: Explicit boundary: judging whether prosody fits an intent is creative/perceptual judgement. Resources supplies the recordings and the declared conditions only.
why: Depends entirely on the AV pack existing first.

media: AV clips with deterministic introduced offsets
required_metadata: exact introduced offset in milliseconds; original alignment
resources_note: The one speech row with a fully deterministic ground truth — shift the audio by a known amount and you know the answer exactly. It is still blocked, because there is nothing to shift.
why: Cheapest speech capability to measure, and completely blocked by the same empty category.

required_metadata: category, market/language, media type, duration, platform; NO quality label from Resources
label_trust: fresh independent human review, run later by Eval. Public/source preference labels are NOT our creative truth.
independence: brand and campaign level; 20 reserve frozen before any tuning
rights_minimum: explicit licence, creator/brand permission, or first-party. Ad creative is dense third-party IP.
resources_note: Pitt Ads (the obvious public candidate) is blocked on an email/manual-approval gate; AVA is blocked on explicit site terms. Neither blocker is licence silence, so neither is waivable under current policy.
why: Both Eval's creative evaluator and Canon's value-gate experiment depend on this one bank. It is the highest-leverage missing pack.

required_metadata: as_REQ-CAP-29
why: Same bank; a separate measurement, not a separate acquisition.

required_metadata: as_REQ-CAP-29
why: Same bank.

target_quantity: shares the video half of the 60 active assets
required_metadata: as REQ-CAP-29 plus duration and platform cut
resources_note: Video ad creative is the hardest half of this bank to licence. If only the static half is obtainable, say so and measure 29-31 rather than pretending 32 is covered.
why: Same bank; the video-specific measurement.

required_metadata: attempt id, repeat index, per-attempt outcome
resources_note: No media to acquire, but it DOES create a Resources obligation: every repeat is an irreproducible output that must be archived under storage class C, or pass-at-k cannot be recomputed later.
why: Reliability is measured over the project's own attempts.

required_metadata: per-attempt cost reference; accepted/not-accepted outcome
resources_note: Cost per Accepted Outcome is the project's primary metric, and it is only recomputable if BOTH the cost reference and the accept/reject outcome survive next to the output bytes. That is a storage-schema requirement, and it is met by EMPIRICAL-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST-SCHEMA.yaml.
why: The metric the whole product optimises. Needs no media and total archive discipline.

required_metadata: API status, error code, refusal text, latency
resources_note: A refusal produces NO output bytes but is still evidence. The archive schema therefore allows a record with a null output hash and a populated api_status — otherwise refusals would vanish from the record and reliability would be overstated.
why: Refusals and errors are part of what a workflow costs.

required_metadata: seed/settings where exposed; version pin; repair attempt chain
resources_note: This row is effectively a test of Resources' own archive. If provenance is incomplete, this capability becomes unmeasurable regardless of the model.
why: Repairability is what turns a failed generation into a cheap retry instead of a lost job.

media: real photographed Devanagari + rendered exactness batteries
target_quantity: Devanagari: existing pools + frozen 96-item battery. Latin: pack to be constructed.
required_metadata: transcription per item; known match/mismatch label by construction
label_trust: battery labels are deterministic by construction; source transcriptions are observations
independence: source lineage — CVIT pair is one lineage; calibration and qualification pools must not share base words or parent photographs
resources_note: THE ONLY EVALUATOR FAMILY WITH SUFFICIENT MATERIAL TODAY. Everything else is partial or blocked.
why: Reading and exactness are the two abilities this family needs, and both have material.

required_metadata: generated ground truth per fixture; unsupported-parse negative controls
resources_note: Resources supplies nothing and should not be asked to. Recorded so this family is not mistaken for a gap.
why: Deterministic truth removes the need for both humans and acquisition.

media: controlled product and person reference packs
target_quantity: >=48 product + >=32 person references, with known-match, known-nonmatch and controlled edit cases
required_metadata: identity/product id; match label by construction; adjudication protocol for similarity
label_trust: match/nonmatch deterministic; degree of similarity is NOT and needs human adjudication
independence: identity and product level between calibration and qualification
geo_language: South Asian representation required for person pack
blocked_reason: Both reference packs are missing and acquiring either requires Controller-approved capture or sourcing strategy. Person capture additionally requires consent that only a human can obtain.
why: This family qualifies the instrument behind 8 capability rows. It is the biggest single unlock in the matrix.

media: clean base clips + deterministic perturbations; identity/text drift cases
target_quantity: perturbation base: existing clips. Drift cases: need reference packs.
required_metadata: introduced perturbation type and magnitude; clip-level observation rule
resources_note: Partially unblockable TONIGHT in design terms: discontinuity, text-instability and continuity perturbations can be built on clips we already hold. Identity-swap/drift cases cannot, because they need the person pack.
why: The only blocked family with a genuine partial path forward using existing material.

media: clean AV clips with transcripts and turn boundaries

label_trust: deterministic for introduced perturbations; verified transcripts otherwise
rights_minimum: media rights AND voice/identity permission, recorded separately
blocked_reason: The corpus contains no audio whatsoever. Nothing can be perturbed, calibrated or qualified until PACK-AV-CLEAN exists.
why: Hardest blocked family: it needs new recording or permissioned material, plus transcript and turn annotation.

required_metadata: descriptive axes only from Resources; creative judgement supplied later by independent human review
label_trust: public/source preference labels are explicitly NOT our creative truth
independence: brand and campaign level; 20-asset reserve frozen before any tuning
blocked_reason: No commercial creative bank exists; the two public candidates are blocked on an access gate and on explicit site terms respectively.
why: Shared with Canon C10. Also the family with the strongest circularity risk, which is why Resources must supply the assets and never the quality labels.

required_metadata: n/a
why: Briefs are written by Canon. Recorded explicitly so no acquisition is proposed against it.

required_metadata: n/a
resources_note: No media, but ~200 model outputs. If those outputs are ever to be re-analysed, they are class C and belong in the empirical archive.
why: Planning lift is measured on text artefacts, not media.

target_quantity: the SAME 60 active assets as REQ-INS-06
required_metadata: descriptive_axes_only
label_trust: independent human review, not Resources labels, not source labels
resources_note: EXPLICIT ANTI-DUPLICATION ROW. Canon C10 and Eval E3 family 6 must consume one bank. Two banks would double the cost and make the two results non-comparable.
why: Canon's value-gate experiment and Eval's creative evaluator ask different questions of identical material.

media: mixed; mostly Eval-constructed, plus reference packs for compound items
required_metadata: per-item measurement fan-out list
independence: base items must not be reused as repeats
resources_note: Of the 10 compound scenario families, 6 require a reference or AV pack that does not exist (packshot, person+product, reference edit, actor+product, one speaker, two-speaker dialogue). Those items can be DESIGNED tonight but cannot be RUN.
why: Tells the Controller exactly how much of the benchmark bank is executable today, which is roughly the atomic half.

independence: briefs from Canon's bank, not authored by Eval

why: The end-to-end run the whole programme builds towards.

media: irreproducible model outputs from Eval runs and production failures
required_metadata: trial id, item id, provider/model/version/endpoint, prompt/config hashes, seed, timestamps, output hash, cost refs, api status, evaluator refs
label_trust: Resources stores evidence; Eval owns interpretation. Resources never decides the failure label.
independence: regression items must be traceable to the exact conditions that produced them
rights_minimum: project-owned outputs; third-party reference material inside them inherits its pack rights
resources_note: The one legacy pool with real recovered evidence: 64 human pass/fail judgements with notes, plus 129 cost lines, recovered from git history tonight. The 64 IMAGES themselves are not in git and are metadata_only.
why: A production failure that is not preserved with its exact conditions cannot become a regression test.
